title: Consonant blends (CCVC/CVCC)
examples: Teacher, what is the difference between a blend and a digraph?
Can you show me some words with 'st' at the beginning?
How do I know when to use a blend instead of a digraph?

explain.say: Today we are learning about consonant blends and digraphs. Say 'st' like you are saying the sound.
A blend is when two consonant sounds go together. Say 'fr' like you are saying the sound.
Sometimes we see '-nd' at the end of a word. Say 'hand' to hear the blend. It sounds like two sounds together.
Another blend is '-mp' at the end. Say 'lamp' to hear the blend. The sounds stay separate.
A digraph is when two letters make one new sound. Say 'sh' like you are saying the sound. It is one sound.
Look at this. 'st' is a blend because you hear two sounds. 'sh' is a digraph because you hear one sound.

faq.q: What is the difference between a blend and a digraph?
faq.a: In a blend, you can hear two separate consonant sounds. In a digraph, two letters make one single new sound.
asks: How do I tell if it is a blend or a digraph?

faq.q: Do all blends have to be at the beginning of a word?
faq.a: No, blends can happen at the beginning, middle, or end of a word. They just need to be together.
asks: Can blends be at the end?
Where can I find consonant blends?

faq.q: Is 'th' a blend or a digraph?
faq.a: The letters 'th' usually make one sound, so it is a digraph. You hear one sound when you say it.

faq.q: How many sounds are in the blend 'bl'?
faq.a: The blend 'bl' has two distinct sounds. You can hear the 'b' sound and the 'l' sound separately.
asks: Can you say the sounds in 'bl'?

faq.q: What is the difference between 'c' and 'ck'?
faq.a: The letter 'c' makes one sound. The letters 'ck' together usually make one sound too. They are different patterns.

facts: A blend keeps the sounds of each letter separate.
A digraph combines two letters to make one sound.
Blends can include sounds like st, fr, bl, or tr.
Digraphs are pairs like sh, ch, or th.

quiz.why: You can hear the /s/ sound and the /t/ sound separately.

wrong.0: This is wrong because a digraph makes only one sound.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the two sounds are clearly separate.
wrong.2: This is wrong because 's' and 't' are both consonant sounds.

quiz.say: Which word has a digraph sound?
quiz.why: In 'ship', the 'sh' makes one single sound, which is a digraph.

wrong.1: This has the blend 'st', which makes two sounds.
wrong.2: This has the blend 'fr', which makes two sounds.
wrong.3: This has the blend 'nd', which makes two sounds.

quiz.say: If you see 'mp' at the end of a word, it is most likely a:
quiz.why: The 'm' sound and the 'p' sound are separate, so it is a blend.

wrong.0: A digraph must make only one sound, not two.
wrong.1: Vowel pairs involve letters like 'ee' or 'oa'.
wrong.2: A silent letter makes no sound at all.
